# 油價續跌帶動債市，AbbVie吸引$630億訂單

## 第二天的反彈，更明顯反映在通膨定價

荷莫茲海峽可能展開掃雷，讓投資人對石油供應恢復有了更具體的期待，美債連續第二天上漲。伊朗正考慮讓歐洲國家參與，卡達表示相關提案已送交各方，美國官員則指出協議可能即將達成。WTI再跌6.41%至$75.19，布蘭特再跌5.96%至$78.78。

5年期及10年期美債殖利率各下降7個基點至4.33%、4.63%；2年期下降5個基點至4.20%，30年期下降5個基點至5.18%。這次10年期漲勢中，通膨補償的貢獻更大：損益兩平通膨率下降4個基點至2.23%，週一僅降1個基點。實質殖利率也下降，但油價持續回落，已更明顯影響市場對通膨及聯準會緊縮幅度的預期。

信用買盤也回來了，卻不是每個借款人都願意接受投資人的條件。AbbVie為收購籌資發行$100億債券，最高吸引約$630億訂單。相較之下，Baker Tilly放棄約$30億貸款，原本計畫用於再融資並支付最多$10億股利。大型製藥商的強勁需求，與買方對股東配息融資的抵制，可以同時出現在公債殖利率下降的一天。

外交進展畢竟仍是提案，海峽尚未恢復正常通行。美國國內通膨也仍高於目標，財政部隔天就將公布季度再融資安排。這波漲勢減輕了能源與預期緊縮帶來的眼前負擔，但長端殖利率仍高於一週及一個月前。

## 市場下修升息幅度，等待季度再融資

5至10年期漲勢最強，2s10s收窄2個基點至43，2s30s維持98。近一週2年期殖利率已下降6個基點，10年期仍上升2個基點，30年期仍升9個基點。近一個月升幅則由2年期的6個基點，擴大至10年期14個基點、30年期20個基點。因此，短端收復先前失地的程度，仍高於長債。

10年期名目殖利率下降7個基點，其中損益兩平通膨率下降4個基點，實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.40%。週一漲勢主要來自實質殖利率，週二則在油價再度重挫、海峽可能建立掃雷機制後，出現更大的通膨補償調整。對船公司及保險業而言，這比單純期待談判更接近可行的航運安全安排。

障礙仍不少。要清出中央航道，仍須安全保證、持久停火，以及伊朗革命衛隊同意；水道治理與收費問題也未解決。市場提高了能源衝擊減輕的可能性，並非已取得正常通航的確認。

短率期貨仍計入9月約15個基點緊縮，年底前完整計入一次25個基點升息，但上週一度還反映兩次升息。油價下降減少第二輪通膨風險，也降低政策必須長期維持限制性的可能。6月職缺降幅亦大於預期，不過市場反應有限，週五就業報告仍是接下來更重要的勞動市場事件。

費城聯準銀行總裁Anna Paulson認為政策略具限制性，並說明了她為何仍可能支持觀望或加碼緊縮：如果基礎通膨繼續改善，目前設定可能足夠；但過去一年進展有限，也可能代表限制程度不足。她估計基礎通膨介於2.4%至2.8%，仍高於2%目標。6月PCE物價下降0.1%時，實質消費卻增加0.4%，國內需求比單看物價數據所呈現的更強。

實質殖利率也反映問題尚未完全化解。10年期收在2.40%，僅比一週前低1個基點，仍比一個月前高14個基點。30年期實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.96%，近一個月仍升17個基點。即使連續兩天債券報酬改善，長期投資的融資成本依然偏高。

週三債務管理指引可能成為下一個影響長端的因素。交易商預期8至10月名目付息券及浮動利率債規模不變，但首次增加規模的預測，從2027年2月到8月都有。部分機構主張，應從「至少未來幾季維持不變」的承諾中刪去「至少」。這種細微措辭，即使不改變下一季標售，也可能讓市場認為調整時間更近。它與聯準會是否實現目前較小的升息循環，是兩個不同問題。

## AbbVie完成發行，Baker Tilly選擇撤案

LQD上漲0.61%，HYG上漲0.30%，JNK上漲0.31%，扭轉週一未跟隨公債反彈的情況。中長期美債漲勢強勁，LQD的漲幅也較大。初級市場結果則更具體顯示，投資人願意把新資金交給誰。

AbbVie發行$100億債券，分成9個券別、年期由2年至40年，協助支付尚未完成的$109億Apogee Therapeutics收購案。最高訂單約$630億，超過AbbVie今年2月$80億發行時的約$390億需求，也略高於Amazon上個月$250億發行所獲訂單。最長券別以美債加92個基點定價，比初步討論收窄33個基點。當日6家投資級發行人合計籌得$173億。

這筆交易也提供了分散風險的機會。它是今年少數不屬於AI借款潮的巨額發行，資金用於成熟製藥公司的收購。在科技供給龐大的背景下，投資組合可以增加部位，不必再承擔一筆晶片價值、資料中心合約或AI交易對手集中度風險。訂單簿顯示這個發行人與這筆交易的承接能力，不代表所有資金用途都能獲得同等需求。

Baker Tilly則無法談妥可接受的價格。這家會計師事務所原擬以約$30億槓桿貸款，置換私募信貸並支付股利，但部分買方要求更高利差，交易因而撤回。配息最多可能達$10億，將是今年非投資級市場最大一筆。由於是趁機改善融資條件，而非迫近到期日的救急，公司可以選擇等待，不必接受當下報價。

這與救援融資失敗不同。把直接放款人的債務轉至聯貸市場，原可能降低借款成本，但加上大額股東分配，就使條件對貸款人較不吸引。近期借款人透過提高成本、加強文件保障或限制資金外流來維持融資；Baker Tilly撤案則顯示，即使債券價格改善，原定交易條件仍未跨過買方門檻。

投資級內部也有壓力。美元及歐元投資級指數中，約$1,000億債券的利差曾高於BB級曲線。Oracle與Stellantis是受到關注的潛在墮落天使，但原因不同：Oracle的資料中心支出引發資本密集度疑慮，Stellantis則面對競爭及營運壓力。若降評，只能持有投資級債券的帳戶可能被迫賣出，由規模較小的高收益買方承接。

這項比較不代表一定會降評。Oracle在7月一度超過BB級利差後，8月初已回到其內側。評等分析師衡量收入、利潤率、現金流與槓桿的時間尺度，也比每日市場定價更長。不過，如此龐大的債券規模跨越這條界線，仍顯示戰爭影響、融資成本及投資需求，正在改變原本穩定信用的交易條件。

另一筆巨額AI融資也逐漸成形。Blackstone已就至少$360億債務接觸投資人，用於Anthropic使用Google晶片，規模可能超過幾個月前完成的約$350億方案。第一筆交易由Broadcom為最大優先順位部分提供付款支持。第二筆將要求投資人再增加對具增信安排晶片租賃、以及仍消耗現金客戶的曝險，投資組合容量與交易對手集中度因此都會影響價格。

洛杉磯的長期資金需求則完全不同。一條1916年鋪設的幹管破裂後，市府計畫發行$4億水務收益債，支應截至2031財政年度逾$100億支出。社區主要管線逾30%已超過80年。穆迪給予Aa3、惠譽AA-，雖有龐大穩定客戶群，野火訴訟仍限制信用。必要公共服務支撐收入，但老舊設施與法律責任同樣需要這些現金。

## 歐洲吸引配置，日本標售需求疲弱

部分經理人正由美債、英國公債及日本公債，轉向歐元區債券，看重相對可預測的制度與政策架構。德國10年期殖利率高於3%，交換市場又計入積極的ECB緊縮，即使認為央行不會完全照此升息的投資人，也因此看到較好的進場價格。美債價格反彈，不必然代表長期配置需求已恢復。

歐洲仍有自己的風險。能源曝險、國防支出及人口老化，對各國預算造成不同負擔。義大利預算協商仍是疑慮，法國10年期債比德國高近80個基點，也部分反映財政及政治差異。先前研究所見的家庭需求受抑，若因持久的荷莫茲協議而恢復信心，也可能減弱，抵銷部分能源降價帶來的通膨紓解。

日本10年期公債標售，需求為2025年5月以來最弱。國內殖利率持續波動，日本銀行仍可能再升息，使本國與海外債券之間的選擇更複雜。干預日圓可降低進口通膨，FIMA融資也能限制被迫賣出美債，但兩者都無法消除更高日本殖利率的相對吸引力。

美國收盤後公布的6月薪資數據，進一步強化這項政策拉力。名目及基本薪資年增率均為3.4%，穩定的全職員工指標增加2.9%，實質薪資增加1.7%，連續第6個月成長。名目增幅高於3%已持續5個月，為34年來最長。對後續交易日而言，這些數據支持日本銀行未來幾個月再升息的可能，也使稍早疲弱的標售更值得關注。

亞洲開發銀行的預測修正，顯示能源衝擊已在區域內留下多少影響。它把亞洲及太平洋開發中經濟體2026年成長預估由5.1%降至4.9%，通膨由3.6%升至4.3%。能源進口國已出現減產及家庭需求轉弱；較低的即期油價改善未來展望，卻不會立即逆轉累積效果。

印度存款流入也正在帶動境外借款。銀行今年已取得$127億境外貸款，2026年剩餘期間可能再籌最多$300億，使全年接近紀錄$430億。銀行及國營金融機構另可能在已發行$108億國際債券之外，再增加最多$100億。

活動主因是銀行競逐利率高於7%的海外印度人外幣存款，部分銀行可放款至原始存款的19倍。安排擴大了美元融資及中介活動，但評估穩定性時，不能只看流入金額，也須考量背後槓桿與再融資需求。前次報告提到的國內流動性支持，只是這個更大資金結構的一部分。

## 新興債反彈，部分央行仍須對抗通膨

美債殖利率下降，帶動EMB上漲0.50%、15年期以上新興市場美元主權債指數上漲0.66%。美元指數僅跌0.09%至99.873，因此共同支撐主要來自美債利率，而非大幅匯率變動。長天期主權債指數近一週仍跌0.46%、一個月仍跌2.90%。

對能源進口國而言，油價降低有利家庭購買力，也減輕政府支持措施成本。但生產中斷、已付出的燃料支出及第二輪通膨，不會隨單日結算價消失。馬達加斯加正顯示這種落差：央行把政策利率由12%提高至12.5%，為一年多來首次升息。

決策者將年底通膨預估由9.3%升至10.1%，認為第2季貨幣條件限制程度不足，並維持5%中期目標。當時油價已因和平希望回到接近$80，央行卻仍須回應累積的通膨展望，而非只看正在逆轉的全球商品價格。

辛巴威的新進展則在債權人協調，而非交易價格。法國與英國將領導債務諮詢小組，首次會議將處理估計$213億公共債務。成立這個論壇，是協調官方債權人與積欠款項的一步，尚不等於各方已同意減債，也不代表市場融資重新開放。對這個借款人而言，債權協商進度比單日美債反彈更直接。

## 科技股大漲，避險需求仍在

S&P 500上漲1.79%，創收盤新高；Nasdaq 100上漲3.32%，半導體指數大漲6.55%。低油價減輕能源成本，低殖利率有利存續期間較長的股票，良好財報也提供支撐。股市並非只有一個上漲原因，但整體與債券改善一致，而不是資金逃離疲弱成長。

VIX卻仍上升4.04%至16.50，黃金上漲2.33%至$4,127.80，顯示股市創高之際仍有避險需求。相較其他資產，美元僅跌0.09%，並不需要以美元條件全面寬鬆來解釋此次復甦。

投資級與高收益基金這次都上漲，不同於週一；但Baker Tilly撤案，仍說明次級市場價格改善不必然能促成每一筆初級交易。跨資產的眼前能源風險降低了，防範逆轉的需求與對個別融資條件的審視卻沒有消失。

## 荷莫茲提案之後，要看實際通航

荷莫茲的下一步是實際通行，而不是再多一項外交樂觀表態。歐洲參與掃雷、伊朗提供保證、革命衛隊同意及持久停火，才能使航運與保險條件正常化。治理、收費或海軍安全爭議仍可能打斷過程。油價連續兩天大跌後，後續進展或逆轉，都會直接影響通膨補償及目前縮小的聯準會升息預期。

美國日程先迎來8月5日季度再融資公告。交易商將觀察，財政部是否維持名目付息券與浮動利率債「至少未來幾季」規模穩定，或開始為2027年較早增發預作準備。真正的標售需求，要等交易發生才能判斷；眼前問題是財政部會提前多久發出供給調整訊號。

週五7月就業報告，接著把焦點轉回國內需求。招聘與薪資相關指標若強勁，即使油價下降，也會支持Paulson對政策限制程度可能不足的疑慮；勞動需求放緩則提供更多觀望理由。這對近期漲勢尤其重要：損益兩平通膨率已反映更多能源紓解，實質殖利率卻仍明顯高於一個月前。

市場仍計入9月約15個基點緊縮、年底前一次完整升息，但上週曾反映兩次。Paulson認為基礎通膨仍有2.4%至2.8%，週三季度再融資指引也可能改變2027年供給預期。

AbbVie籌得$100億，最高吸引約$630億訂單；Baker Tilly則因買方要求更高利差，撤回約$30億貸款。正在討論的另一筆Anthropic融資規模至少$360億。海外方面，日本疲弱標售及隨後薪資數據，使升息展望持續受到關注；馬達加斯加則在油價下降之際仍提高利率。
overall_summary.summary: 荷莫茲掃雷提案加深油價跌勢，10年期美債殖利率下降7個基點至4.63%。通膨補償與預期升息幅度同步下修；AbbVie發行需求強勁，Baker Tilly卻撤回含股東配息的貸款。

section_summaries.section_title: 第二天的反彈，更明顯反映在通膨定價
section_summaries.summary: 荷莫茲可能建立掃雷安排，帶動油價再度重挫。通膨補償與實質殖利率同步下降，初級信用需求卻因交易而異。

section_summaries.section_title: 市場下修升息幅度，等待季度再融資

# Oil extends its slide as AbbVie draws a $63 billion orderbook

## A second day of relief reaches inflation pricing

Treasuries rallied for a second day as a possible plan to clear mines from the Strait of Hormuz gave investors a more concrete basis for expecting oil supplies to recover. Iran was considering European participation, Qatar said a proposal had circulated, and US officials indicated an agreement could be close. WTI fell another 6.41% to $75.19 and Brent dropped 5.96% to $78.78.

The five- and ten-year Treasury yields each declined 7 basis points, to 4.33% and 4.63%. Two-year yields fell 5 basis points to 4.20%, and the 30-year fell 5 to 5.18%. This time, more of the ten-year rally came through inflation compensation: the breakeven fell 4 basis points to 2.23%, compared with just 1 basis point on Monday. Real yields also declined, but oil's sustained retreat was now making a larger impression on the expected inflation path and the amount of Fed tightening priced into markets.

Credit buyers returned too, though not on terms every borrower would accept. AbbVie's $10 billion acquisition-financing sale drew about $63 billion of peak orders. Baker Tilly, by contrast, abandoned a roughly $3 billion loan that would have refinanced debt and funded a dividend of as much as $1 billion. Demand for a large pharmaceutical issuer and resistance to a sponsor distribution could coexist even as government yields fell.

The diplomacy was still a proposal rather than a reopened waterway. Domestic inflation also remained above target, and Treasury's refunding announcement was a day away. The bond rally reduced the immediate burden from energy and expected policy tightening, while leaving the long end above its week- and month-earlier levels.

## Markets trim expected hikes ahead of refunding

The strongest gains were in five- to ten-year maturities. The 2s10s curve flattened 2 basis points to 43, while 2s30s stayed at 98. Over a week, the two-year yield was down 6 basis points, but the ten-year was still up 2 and the 30-year up 9. Monthly increases ranged from 6 basis points at two years to 14 at ten and 20 at 30. The recent recovery has thus been more complete at the front end than in long bonds.

At ten years, the 7-basis-point nominal decline split into a 4-basis-point fall in the breakeven and a 3-basis-point fall in the real yield to 2.40%. Monday's nominal rally had been dominated by real yields. Tuesday's larger adjustment in inflation compensation followed a second steep oil decline and a possible mechanism for making Hormuz safer for shipping and insurers.

Several obstacles remained. Clearing a central channel would require security assurances, a durable ceasefire and agreement from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Governance of the waterway and fee collection were still disputed. Markets were assigning greater weight to a reduction in the energy shock, not trading on confirmation that normal traffic had resumed.

Short-rate futures retained about 15 basis points of September tightening and one full 25-basis-point increase by year-end, down from two increases priced as recently as last week. Lower oil reduces the risk of second-round inflation and the need to keep policy restrictive for longer. June job openings also fell more than expected, although that release elicited little market reaction; Friday's employment report remained the more important labor-market event ahead.

Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson described policy as mildly restrictive and set out why she could still favor either patience or additional restraint. Current settings might be sufficient if underlying inflation continued to improve; limited progress over the past year could instead mean they were not restrictive enough. Her estimate of underlying inflation was 2.4%–2.8%, above the 2% target. June's 0.1% fall in PCE prices had come alongside a 0.4% increase in real consumption, leaving domestic demand stronger than the inflation headline alone suggested.

Real yields reflected that incomplete resolution. The ten-year real yield at 2.40% was only 1 basis point below its week-earlier level and still 14 basis points higher over a month. The 30-year real yield fell 3 basis points to 2.96%, leaving a 17-basis-point monthly increase. The cost of financing long-lived investment therefore remained high despite two days of better bond returns.

Wednesday's debt-management guidance could become the next influence on those longer maturities. Dealers expected nominal coupon and floating-rate note sizes to stay unchanged for the August-to-October quarter, but forecasts for the first increase ranged from February to August 2027. Some favored removing “at least” from the promise to keep sizes steady for several quarters. A small wording change could shorten the perceived timetable without changing the coming quarter's auctions. The issue is separate from whether the Fed delivers the smaller tightening cycle now priced by markets.

## AbbVie clears; Baker Tilly walks away

LQD rose 0.61%, HYG gained 0.30% and JNK added 0.31%, reversing their failure to join Monday's government-bond rally. LQD's larger gain accompanied the strong move in intermediate and long Treasuries. Primary-market results offered a more specific view of where investors were willing to commit new money.

AbbVie sold $10 billion across nine maturities spanning two to 40 years to help finance its pending $10.9 billion purchase of Apogee Therapeutics. Peak demand of about $63 billion exceeded the roughly $39 billion drawn by AbbVie's $8 billion February sale and slightly surpassed orders for Amazon's $25 billion offering last month. The longest tranche priced 92 basis points over Treasuries, 33 basis points tighter than initial discussion. Six investment-grade issuers raised $17.3 billion in total.

The deal also offered diversification. It was one of the few jumbo sales this year outside the AI borrowing wave, with proceeds tied to an acquisition by an established pharmaceutical company. Portfolios facing a large technology pipeline could add size without taking another position in chip values, data-center contracts or concentrated AI counterparties. The orderbook showed capacity for this issuer and transaction, rather than an equally strong bid for every use of proceeds.

Baker Tilly could not reach an acceptable price. The accounting firm withdrew a roughly $3 billion leveraged loan intended to refinance private credit debt and fund a dividend after some buyers demanded wider spreads. The distribution could have reached $1 billion, the year's largest in non-investment-grade markets. Because the financing was opportunistic rather than a response to an imminent maturity, the company could wait rather than accept those terms.

That choice distinguishes the transaction from a failed rescue. Moving direct-lender debt into the syndicated market might have reduced borrowing costs, but a large payout made the proposition less attractive to lenders. Recent borrowers have preserved access by paying more, strengthening documents or limiting value leakage. Baker Tilly's withdrawal showed the limit of the proposed economics even on a day of improving bond prices.

Pressure was also visible within investment grade. About $100 billion of bonds in dollar and euro investment-grade indexes had traded at spreads wider than the double-B curve. Oracle and Stellantis were prominent potential fallen angels, for different reasons: Oracle's data-center spending raised questions about capital intensity, while Stellantis faced competition and operating pressure. A downgrade could compel investment-grade-only holders to sell into a smaller high-yield investor base.

The comparison was not a prediction of certain downgrades. Oracle's spreads had already moved back inside double-B levels by early August after crossing them in July. Ratings analysts weigh revenue, margins, cash flow and leverage over longer periods than daily market pricing. The size of the cohort nevertheless showed how war effects, financing costs and investment demands were changing the terms on which previously stable credits traded.

Another large AI transaction was taking shape. Blackstone had sounded out investors on at least $36 billion of debt to finance Anthropic's use of Google chips, potentially exceeding the roughly $35 billion package completed a few months earlier. Broadcom backstopped payments on the largest senior portions of that first deal. A second financing would ask investors to add still more exposure to supported chip leases and a cash-burning customer, making both portfolio capacity and counterparty concentration relevant to pricing.

Los Angeles presented a different long-term capital need. The city planned $400 million of water-revenue bonds toward more than $10 billion of spending through fiscal 2031 after a trunk line dating to 1916 ruptured. More than 30% of neighborhood mainlines were over 80 years old. Moody's assigned Aa3 and Fitch AA-, with wildfire litigation constraining the credit despite a large, stable customer base. Essential-service demand supports the revenue stream, but aging infrastructure and legal exposure still compete for that cash.

## Europe attracts allocations as Japan's auction disappoints

Some managers were shifting from Treasuries, gilts and Japanese government bonds toward euro-area debt, attracted by what they saw as a more predictable institutional and policy framework. German ten-year yields above 3% and aggressive ECB tightening priced into swaps had improved entry levels, even for investors who doubted the bank would deliver all of those increases. Better US bond prices did not necessarily imply a recovery in strategic demand for Treasuries.

Europe retained its own risks. Energy exposure, defense spending and aging populations place different burdens on national budgets. Italian budget negotiations remained a concern, while French ten-year debt offered almost 80 basis points over Germany partly because of fiscal and political differences. The demand restraint identified in earlier euro-area research could also weaken if a lasting Hormuz agreement restored household confidence, offsetting part of the disinflationary benefit of lower energy costs.

Japan's ten-year JGB auction drew its weakest demand since May 2025. Domestic yields remained volatile and another BOJ increase was still possible, complicating the decision between local and foreign bonds. Yen intervention can reduce imported inflation, and FIMA funding can limit forced Treasury sales, but neither removes the relative-value attraction of higher Japanese yields.

After the US close, June wage data added to that policy tension. Nominal and base pay each rose 3.4% from a year earlier, the stable full-time measure increased 2.9%, and real wages gained 1.7% for a sixth consecutive month. Nominal gains above 3% had lasted five months, the longest run in 34 years. For the coming sessions, those figures reinforced the case for another BOJ increase and added significance to the earlier weak auction.

The Asian Development Bank's revisions showed how much of the energy shock had already reached the region. It lowered its 2026 growth forecast for developing Asia and the Pacific from 5.1% to 4.9% and raised inflation from 3.6% to 4.3%. Energy-importing economies had experienced production cuts and weaker household demand. Cheaper spot oil improves the outlook without immediately reversing those accumulated effects.

India's deposit inflows were also generating offshore borrowing. Banks were expected to raise as much as $30 billion of offshore loans in the remainder of 2026, after $12.7 billion already secured, potentially taking the annual total near a record $43 billion. Banks and state-owned financiers could add up to $10 billion of global bonds to the $10.8 billion already raised.

Competition for nonresident Indian foreign-currency deposits paying above 7% was driving the activity, with some banks allowed to lend as much as 19 times the original deposit. The arrangement broadens dollar funding and intermediation, but the leverage and need to refinance belong alongside the headline inflow when assessing its stability. The domestic liquidity support described in the previous report is only one part of this larger funding structure.

## EM bonds recover while local inflation still forces action

EMB gained 0.50% and the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index rose 0.66% as US yields fell. The Dollar Index declined only 0.09% to 99.873, leaving lower Treasury yields as a more important common support than a large currency move. The long sovereign index remained down 0.46% over a week and 2.90% over a month.

For energy importers, lower crude helps both household purchasing power and the cost of government support. Yet production disruptions, earlier fuel bills and second-round inflation do not disappear with one settlement price. That lag was visible in Madagascar, whose central bank raised its policy rate from 12% to 12.5%, the first increase in more than a year.

Policymakers raised the year-end inflation forecast from 9.3% to 10.1%, judged second-quarter monetary conditions insufficiently restrictive and retained a 5% medium-term target. The decision came as oil approached $80 on hopes of peace. Local policy was responding to the accumulated inflation outlook, even as the global commodity shock began to reverse.

Zimbabwe's development concerned creditor coordination rather than traded prices. France and the UK were set to lead a Debt Consultative Group, with its first meeting due to address estimated public debt of $21.3 billion. Establishing the forum is a step toward reconciling official creditors and arrears; it is not yet an agreed reduction in debt or a reopening of market access. For this borrower, progress depends more directly on the creditor process than on a single day's Treasury rally.

## Technology surges, with hedging demand still visible

The S&P 500 gained 1.79% to a record close, the Nasdaq 100 rose 3.32% and semiconductors jumped 6.55%. Lower oil reduced the energy burden and lower yields helped longer-duration equities, while solid earnings also supported the advance. The stock rally had more than one driver, but it was consistent with the improvement in bonds rather than a flight from weakening growth.

VIX nevertheless rose 4.04% to 16.50, and gold gained 2.33% to $4,127.80. Hedging demand remained visible alongside record equities. The dollar's 0.09% decline was small relative to the moves elsewhere, so a broad easing in dollar conditions was not necessary to explain the recovery.

Investment-grade and high-yield funds both advanced, unlike Monday, but the canceled Baker Tilly financing showed why better secondary prices need not secure every primary deal. Across assets, the immediate energy risk had diminished; protection against a reversal and scrutiny of individual financing terms remained in place.

## From a Hormuz proposal to shipping access

The next step in Hormuz is physical access, not another expression of diplomatic optimism. European demining participation, Iranian assurances, IRGC consent and a durable ceasefire would allow shipping and insurance conditions to normalize. Disputes over governance, fees or naval security could still interrupt that process. After two days of steep crude declines, progress—or its reversal—has direct implications for inflation compensation and the smaller Fed tightening cycle now priced.

The August 5 refunding announcement arrives first on the US calendar. Dealers will watch whether Treasury retains “at least several quarters” of stable nominal coupon and floating-rate note sizes, or begins preparing for an earlier 2027 increase. Auction demand can only be assessed when the sales take place; the immediate issue is how much warning Treasury gives about future supply.

Friday's July employment report then turns attention back to domestic demand. Firm hiring and wage-sensitive measures would support Paulson's concern that mildly restrictive policy may not be enough, even with lower oil. Softer labor demand would provide more reason to wait. The distinction matters after the recent rally: breakevens now reflect greater energy relief, while real yields remain substantially above month-earlier levels.
